change_summary: The editors issued an expression of concern because they had received concerns about the calculation of the dose-response analysis and were investigating, and following that investigation the article was retracted and replaced by a corrected version. The retraction notice says the Table 3 dose-response slope was miscalculated: it was reported as 0.45 points per 10 mg, and the correct value is 0.28. The stored paper gave the slope's 95% confidence interval as 0.30 to 0.60, while the corrected version gives it as 0.15 to 0.41. The notice states that the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged, and the corrected version still concludes that the reduction in fatigue increased with the daily dose between 20 and 60 mg, so the size of the dose-response effect changed while the direction of the main finding stands.
evaluation: Your Discussion compares your slope of 0.41 fatigue points per 10 mg with the 0.45 per 10 mg of Park and Singh [7], and says this closeness supports the validity of your design. The stored paper reported a slope of 0.45 points per 10 mg (95% CI 0.30 to 0.60), but the retraction notice says this was miscalculated and the correct value is 0.28, and the corrected version gives the confidence interval as 0.15 to 0.41. The comparison in your Discussion rests on the 0.45 slope, which the notice corrects to 0.28, so this use is touched, and your 0.41 now equals the upper limit of the corrected interval. The notice states that the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged, and because the affected use is a comparison, the impact on your draft is low.
recommendation: Your Discussion compares your slope of 0.41 fatigue points per 10 mg with the 0.45 per 10 mg of Park and Singh [7], and says this closeness supports the validity of your design. The retraction notice says the Table 3 slope was miscalculated and the correct value is 0.28 points per 10 mg, and the corrected version gives the confidence interval as 0.15 to 0.41, so your 0.41 equals the upper limit of the corrected interval. The article was retracted and replaced by a corrected version, and the notice states that the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged. Update the Discussion sentence to the corrected 0.28 slope and cite the corrected version and the notice; check whether the comparison still supports the validity of your design, and reword it if not.
